answer.answerText:
**No.** Four bottle-filling stations cannot replace all four required drinking fountains. Where drinking fountains are required, only **up to 50 percent** may be substituted with dedicated container-filling fixtures; therefore, at most **two** of the four required fountains may be replaced, and at least **two drinking fountains** must remain. Each substituted fixture must be adjacent to or readily visible from a drinking fountain that conforms to PC 410.1. (PC § 410.3)

Further, drinking fountains required by Table 403.1 must have both a bubbler faucet and a separate container-filling faucet. Thus, for this four-fountain requirement, the compliant baseline is two conforming drinking fountains—each with both functions—and no more than two qualifying dedicated bottle-filling fixtures. (PC § 410.1)

answer.answerText:
**No.** An ordinary shutoff valve cannot be the sole bulkhead between gas in one piping section and test medium in an adjacent section. FGC § 406.1.4 states: “Under no circumstances shall a valve in a line be used as a bulkhead” in that situation, except where **a double block and bleed valve system or flange** is installed. A valve also cannot be subjected to test pressure unless the piping upstream of it has been deenergized; the portion not pressure-tested must be checked with a noncorrosive leak-detecting fluid or another approved leak-detecting method. (FGC § 406.1.4)

Before acceptance and initial operation, all piping installations must be inspected and pressure-tested for code-compliant materials, design, fabrication, and installation practices (FGC § 406.1); before being placed in service, piping must be tested gas-tight and its testing, inspection, and purging must comply with FGC § 406 (FGC § 404.20). For a completed section test, the test-pressure source must be isolated before testing. (FGC § 406.4)
answer.conclusion: **No.** An ordinary shutoff valve cannot be the sole bulkhead between gas in one piping section and test medium in an adjacent section. FGC § 406.1.4 states: “Under no circumstances shall a valve in a line be used as a bulkhead” in that situation, except where **a double block and bleed valve system or flange** is installed. A valve also cannot be subjected to test pressure unless the piping upstream of it has been deenergized; the portion not pressure-tested must be checked with a noncorrosive leak-detecting fluid or another approved leak-detecting method. (FGC § 406.1.4)

No. Even if the domestic-water pipe is strong enough, the 2022 NYC Fuel Gas Code expressly provides that gas piping “shall not be supported by other piping.” The gas piping must instead be supported by an allowed metal support, hanger, bracket, band, hook, or building structural component suitable for the pipe size and of adequate strength and quality, installed at intervals that prevent or damp out excessive vibration. It must also be anchored to prevent undue strain on connected appliances, and the supports must comply with the stated installation conditions. (FGC § 407.2)

answer.answerText:
**No.** For the ordinary same-room appliance-shutoff path, the valve must be within 6 feet of the appliance; at 8 feet, it exceeds that limit by 2 feet. Each appliance must have a shutoff valve complying with either FGC § 409.5.1 or § 409.5.2. FGC § 409.5.1 also requires the valve to be upstream of the union, connector, or quick-disconnect device it serves, accessible, and generally no more than 60 inches above the finished floor (with the stated elevated-connection exception). (FGC §§ 409.5, 409.5.1)

A different result is possible only if this is a vented decorative appliance, room heater, or decorative appliance installed in a vented fireplace and the remote-valve conditions of FGC § 409.5.2 are met: ready access, permanent identification, service to no other appliance, and compliant piping from the valve to within 6 feet of the appliance. The stated absence of a special manifold arrangement does not change the ordinary 6-foot rule.

The duct should therefore continue to an outdoor termination, located so the exhaust will not cause a nuisance or be readily drawn back into a ventilating system.
